# Parental Leave Policy

## Eligibility

All full-time employees who have completed at least 90 days of continuous
employment are eligible for paid parental leave. This applies equally to
birth parents, adoptive parents, and foster parents. Part-time employees
working 20 or more hours per week are eligible for a pro-rated benefit.

## Duration and Pay

Eligible employees receive 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave. Leave can
be taken in a single continuous block or split into two blocks within the
first 12 months after the birth, adoption, or foster placement, subject to
manager approval. Pay continues at 100% of base salary during the leave
period; variable pay such as commissions or bonuses is calculated separately
under the standard compensation plan.

## Requesting Leave

Employees should notify their manager and HR at least 30 days before the
expected start date where possible. For births, submit the request as soon
as the due date is known. HR will confirm the leave dates in writing and
coordinate the return-to-work plan.

## Job Protection and Benefits Continuation

Health insurance and other benefits continue uninterrupted during parental
leave, with the company covering its usual share of premiums. Employees are
guaranteed the right to return to the same or an equivalent role with the
same pay, benefits, and seniority.

## Extending Leave

Employees who want additional unpaid leave beyond the 16 weeks may request
up to 8 additional weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave, subject to HR
approval and business needs.
